The closure day for Founding member applications for the EEHP is over! This shall mark the debates on the terms of each point. For simplicity and speed, [b][i][u]THIS WILL NOT BE IN RP COMMUNICATION.[/u][/i][/b] Each point will be debated until a reasonable agreement can be made, and then the discussion will be put to the second point. After debating the five original points, there will be a time where nations can discuss any points they would like to add, and those will be put to a vote. Let the debate begin! 

For a reminder, these are the points:
[b][i]1.[/i][/b] Open borders and ports: The members of the EEHP will share open borders with each other. In practice, this means citizens of each nation will have the privilege of traveling passport and visa free, with the potential of streamlined immigration between members. This brings the benefit of increased tourism and a larger sense of collaboration between members. Members will also have open port policies with the other members, meaning a decrease in docking fees allowing for ease of business between members.

[b][i]2.[/i][/b] Sharing of business licenses and integration of international safety standards:Members of the EEHP will share the same level of safety standards and regulations, thus allowing for companies to be licensed in one country and use that license across all nations in the EEHP rather than having to get multiple licenses and concern themselves with different laws and safety standards. This will not only help companies, but also ensure that ethical practices in EEHP countries will be encouraged.

[b][i]3.[/i][/b] Sharing of innovations and breakthroughs: EEHP members will share practices with each other to not only benefit members, but also build a better Erene for current and future generations. This includes the sharing of the best industry practices to prevent environmental impact via pollution, deforestation, over-farming/fishing, and also share stake in world wide conservation projects of natural habitats and cultural sites. Breakthroughs in industries will also be shared between nations, allowing for better industry practices across the world.

[b][i]4.[/i][/b] Implement tariffs and import restrictions on nations that promote unethical practices or undemocratic principles: Membership in the EEHP not only looks to benefit the nations in it, but to benefit the world via lowering and hopefully removing reliance on fascist nations or those ruled by dictators (not including constitutional monarchies, parliamentary monarchies, or similar governments that practice the basics of democracy and good humanitarian practices.) Stemming the reliance on child labor and the exploitation of workers via taxing the imports from these nations will hopefully encourage the nations that use these practices to pivot to more sustainable and humanitarian based practices. The first and second points of this charter will also help ease the transition from the companies that use these practices by making the shipment of resources between members cheaper and more accessible to companies in the member nations.

[b][i]5.[/i][/b] Promotion of humanitarian practices: Humanitarian laws to be practiced and imposed in member nations include but are not limited to:
- Laws against exclusion of people based on their race, gender, sexuality, or religion
- Freedom of religion
- Freedom of speech (specifics to be determined by the founding members)
- Minimum wage laws (to be determined by the individual country)
- Limit on maximum hours of work before overtime pay begins
- Free school for at least up until grade/year 8 in less developed countries, and free high school for the more developed countries (university/college is up to the individual country to decide)
These policies will be helped via an aid fund to be contributed to by each government via a number of % of their GDP to help other member nations with disasters or modernization

[b][i]Additional Clause:[/i][/b]
Membership is not restricted to these nations and the ULR encourages people to apply for membership, this list is simply a list of countries the ULR knows are respectable and has good relations with already. It should also be clarified that this will not interject with any military alliances, however if one member attacks another, or a nation attacks a member and another member state joins the attack, the attacking member will be removed from the pact if the member does not provide ample reason for such action.

[quote=norrhollow;59101043][b]11 April 2025

SummitONE Solutions

Memorandum

Subject: Developments and Projects in Sal-Baliz[/b]

[list]

[i]WARNING

This document contains information that may or may not concern the strategic interests of the Commonwealth of High Albany and is subject to Chapter 7, section 7.3, of the SummitONE Code of Ethics and Conduct, as amended. The transmission, distribution, or duplication of this memorandum by unauthorized persons or entities is prohibited under law.[/i]

[/list]

[b]I. RECENT EVENTS[/b]

1. Much has transpired in the interim between the initial conclusion of Sal-Baliz's deal with SummitONE and now. With prospects of confederalization from the member states of THEP, SummitONE has reviewed its present resources with the highest scrutiny. Following analysis of preexisting infrastructure, SummitONE has concluded that Sal-Baliz does not presently possess the military capabilities to fend off present enemy offensives on its territory, whether in manpower, material, food and water, and other essential resources. Hence, while corporate resources remain steadfast in honoring our most recent agreement, SummitONE believes that an expansion of present operations will be necessary to ensure the continuation of military resistance.

2. Hydronia, Etherniasti, and Thýven are the three most dangerous opponents of Sal-Baliz at the present. While SummitONE Solutions remains optimistic in the capability of the Corps of Commissionaires in fending off their advance, we are cautiously optimisitc of the capabilities of the Sal-Baliz militias. As it stands, morale among Sal-Baliz forces remains shockingly high and is expected to continue as further foreign encroachment continues in West Shamat. Yet, limitations in the standardization of armaments, poor literacy, superstition, language barriers with SummitONE operatives, and limited understanding of medicine and engineering are severely hampering military efforts. There exists a deep social divide between the most capable of fighters trained to fight with SummitONE vehicles and armaments, versus more traditional guerillas who have yet to fully adapt to SummitONE strategy and tactics.

3. Ulf de Mayne, the current Regional Operations Manager, has expressed discontent with the current state of the conflict. Following the departure of Freya Moran on contact with the Elseyrian branch, the SummitONE command structure has been unnecessarily strained, especially following the deaths of major operatives William Arud and Terrence Alsvik last March. However, following the conclusion of the SummitONE contact in Elseyr, Freya Moran is expected to return to Sal-Baliz soon together with a host of other veterans. The comapny remains hopeful that this injection of fresh reinforcements shall encourage command to operate on a rotational basis to reduce exhaustion and combat fatigue, while also promoting a more sustainable work environment among contractors. Sal-Baliz command remains steadfast and capable due to nature of defensive war, though the company recommends adopting a rotational system as well to ensure that commander of smaller sub-units remain primed and ready during combat.

4. Sal-Baliz losses have been significant throughout the conflict, but SummitONE losses remain low. Apart from the deaths of Commander William Arud and Specialist Terrence Alvik on 28 March 2025, casualties have so far remained minimal thanks to SummitONE prioritization of strategic consultation over frontline involvement. However, as SummitONE expects to increase its operations over the coming months, this trend may not continue for long. We hope to negotiate a larger, more lucrative contract with Sal-Baliz to shoulder the burden of these risks.

[b]II. DEVELOPMENTS AND PROJECTS[/b]

1. At the time of writing, 23 factories have been successfully constructed in Sal-Baliz, the majority constructed near the central territories of the state where they are safest against THEP aerial bombing runs. 3 of these factories are operated directly by SummitONE Technologies for production of terrestrial vehicles, 8 are operated directly by SummitONE Technologies for production of artillery, explosives, and drone technology, 3 are operated partially by SummitONE Intelligence for production of radar and cyberwarfare technologies, while the rest are wholly owned by Sal-Baliz operatives for production of small arms, munitions, and non-lethal material such as body armor, meals-ready-to-eat (MREs), sandbags, gasoline, and combat casualty response kits.

2. Al-Sharwa has been successfully transformed into a comprehensive military compound by SummitONE Technologies and SummitONE Corps of Commissionaires. AOpsMgr. Cedric Falwell currently administers the territory with the supporting of SummitONE's Alpha Company of Commissionaires. As of the moment, the settlement has been repurposed as a training ground for Sal-Baliz operatives aiming to enlist as contractors for the company's training regimen and as a weapons stockpile for tanks, IFVs, and other armored vehicles that have yet to be deployed into the conflict.

3. Around 40 tanks have been produced by SummitONE Technologies, 80% of them from modular assemblies in Norrhollow and 20% from factories within Sal-Baliz. We anticipate numbers to increase to 300 tanks per month once Seagate Zurekdal becomes fully operational. In addition to this, SummitONE has finished producing 800 artillery systems, 3 fighter aircraft, 15 combat helicopters, and an undisclosed number of small arms capable of arming no less than 40% of Sal-Baliz's entire active fighting force in battle. The production of medical kits has been slow in recent weeks due to supply limitations, as have been the production of body armor and other non-lethal material, though these are expected to be alleviated soon.

4. Seagate Zurekdal, a major prefabricated port-building project of SummitONE Seagates, has finished most of its non-military infrastructure. While further infrastructure is still necessary so that the site could be used as a regular naval base, it is now partially capable of serving as a port for SummitONE dark ships to enter and seamlessly ship resources directly to Sal-Baliz. Caisson-based floating platforms have been installed to serve as docking sites for new ships, while solar powered farms and desalination barges help sustain personnel on the Seagate. Barracks, storage facilities, and naval batteries are still in the midst of construction but are expected to be accomplished by the next year. Nuclear microreactors are still pending construction due to delays in material sourcing and bureaucratic scrutiny from the Ministry of Energy.

5. SummitONE Technologies has formulated five sets of MREs to supplant Sal-Baliz's current combat rations: Standard A (Chicken Biryani), Standard B (Lamb Kofta), Standard C (Beef Stew w/ Apricots), Standard D (Falafel & Tabbouleh), and the Mobile Kitchen Module (Beef Keema, Chicken Kabsa, Beef Stew w/ Apricots). The Standard modules each contain approximately 1,2501,300 kcal per meal, 1318% protein, 3035% fat, 5055% carbohydrates, and with essential vitamins and minerals. The Mobile Kitchen Module is of similar composition, but designed to sustain at least 50 operatives per unit. All MREs are expected to last for up to 36 months at 27°C, though modules may last beyond 5 years in refrigeration. All MREs do not require gasoline to heat, instead possessing magnesium-based water-activated tray heaters. All MREs have been independently verified to be halal by the Institute of Culinary Arts at the University of the Hollows, Norrhollow, though additional processing may be undertaken at Sal-Baliz to ensure maximum compliance with religious laws.[/quote]

Supreme leader Falah finds this report satisfactory. Your operatives will be rewarded for their service soon

[spoiler=Expansion : Sakara (3,375 words)]
[i]Sakara, a small kingdom to the west of the powerful expanse of the Holy Hydronic Empire, boasted a rich cultural heritage but suffered for nearly a century under brutal dictatorships and economic turmoil. Its people were known for their artistry, vibrant markets, and laughter echoing through the cobblestone streets that twisted like veins through the heart of the kingdom. In times of prosperity, Sakara stood resilient in the face of foreign dominion, deftly maintaining its sovereignty even as vast empires sought to impose their rule.[/i]

Generations of Sakaras citizens had lived under the gentle embrace of their beloved customs, celebrating the seasons and the land with festivals that brought communities together. Each festival was a reminder of their history, intertwining stories of triumph, love, and identity that enriched the cultural tapestry of their nation. Yet, an undercurrent of vulnerability lingered, as the pressures of modernity encroached upon their way of life, threatening to unravel the very fabric that held them together.

However, this vibrancy began to dim as the years advanced. Descent into chaos was inevitable, as Sakara fell into the grips of brutal dictatorships, crushing the spirit of its citizens and plunging them into economic strife. For almost a century, despair became a familiar blanket that suffocated dreams and hope. The laughter that once filled the streets now morphed into muted whispers and cries of the disenfranchised.

Amidst the backdrop of abandoned shops and desolate squares, families struggled to survive as inflation destabilized their livelihoods. The once-cherished market stalls, brimming with color and life, became hollow shells of past memories, leaving echoes of desperation where prosperity once thrived. Simple joys, like gathering for communal meals, felt like relics of an era long lost to the ruthless grasp of hardship.

The monarchy, once a symbol of unity and hope, became a beacon of oppression, further alienating the people from the cause they once revered. Citizens grew weary of hollow promises made by a succession of self-interested rulers; complacency became a disease that spread among them, and faith in leadership dwindled to near extinction.

A transformative moment arrived with the unexpected death of King Erhan, the last monarch of this beleaguered dynasty. His reign had lasted for decades, dragging Sakara to the precipice of collapse yet again. The ascension of his successor, Aras Kaymakan inexperienced young mandid little to lift the growing weight of despair from the shoulders of Sakaras citizens. Although he inherited the title of king, he also inherited a legacy drenched in hunger, fear, and oppression.

Within days, the burden became apparent. Prices soared, and the population plunged deeper into a chasm of dissatisfaction. Fearful whispers turned into resentful murmurs, and soon, the air crackled with the potential for major upheaval.

Reports of unrest began to filter into the palace corridors, where Aras sat behind gilded walls, wrapped in privilege but ignorant of the cries for justice emanating from beyond his palace gates. Aras initially dismissed the burgeoning protests as the mere grumblings of discontented citizens, unwilling to acknowledge the growing storm that engulfed his kingdom.

But as the days turned into weeks, demonstrators began to gather outside the opulent but increasingly besieged palace. Armed with nothing but their voices, their fists, and whatever means of expression they could muster, they clamored for change that had eluded them for too long. The air thickened with anger as the kings ineffectual regime safeguarded its authority through fear.

Among the ranks of protestors was a middle-aged factory worker named Tuncay Bakkal, known for his outspokenness and deep sense of justice. Tuncay possessed an innate ability to connect with people, understanding their pain and desires better than most. He felt the peoples oppression in his bones and became a rallying point for the desperate masses. Tuncay stood tall amidst the sea of bodies, shouting commands that unified the protestors, igniting a fervor for liberation.

On the day before the uprising erupted, the sense of despair crystallized visiblyabandoned shops, desolate alleyways filled with refuse, families scavenging for scraps. Amid this grim tableau, the citizens found themselves ready to reclaim their lives, their spirits simmering with a potent mix of desperation and resolve.

As midnight drew near, the palace guards found themselves facing an overwhelming tide of protestors, who surged toward the gates, no longer willing to tolerate oppression. Shouting slogans of defiance, they burrowed through the monochrome barriers of authority. Their resolve struck at the heart of the kingdom's leadership.

The moment arrived when the gates of the palace buckled under pressure, allowing demonstrators to flood into the courtyard. In the chaos, determined voices rose above the din, and led by Tuncay, the masses stormed through archways leading to the kings private quarters.

As they descended into the heart of the palace, whispers of fear echoed through its opulencea stark contrast to what lay outside. They finally arrived at the kings office, where Aras sat petrified and shivering, having lost all semblance of control.

ON YOUR KNEES! Tuncay bellowed, weapon raised, channeling the combined desperation of the crowd. The king, stripped of his delusions of dominance, sank to his knees on the plush carpetonce a perch for authoritative decisions.

The palpable tension hung in the air, thickening with each heartbeat, as protestors smashed the glass case housing Sakara's constitution. It was an act of rebellion fueled by anguish, signaling the end of an era and a defiance against tyranny. The flames sparked ominously outside, casting chaotic shadows upon the walls.

With the monarchy's power disassembled, Tuncay emerged as a symbol of hope. In the aftermath, he passionately delivered a speech, unveiling his vision for Sakaraa future anchored in democracy, stability, and a promise for a brighter tomorrow. With fervent determination, he utilized his platform to galvanize a shaken populace, breathing life into their aspirations for change.

As the crowd absorbed his words, a spirit of unity surgedtheir once-imprisoned dreams experienced a resurgence. Tuncays vision was shared fervently, and without hesitation, he spearheaded contact with Hydronia to discuss potential unification.

On April 7, 2025, alongside key allies, Tuncay crossed into Hydronia, filled with hope and apprehension about the future. The transition from despair towards possibility was fraught with uncertainty, but the flicker of determination fueled their ambition.

Upon their arrival in Hydropolis, the negotiation rooms brimmed with possibilities, with powerful figures like President Kaplan Zorlu and Minister of Foreign Affairs Halis Erdermir waiting to engage. The air crackled with anticipation as Tuncay presented the heartfelt plight of his people.

Welcome, Tuncay, President Zorlu acknowledged, noting the urgency etched into the young leader's voice. Weve been following your journey closely. Your peoples cries for freedom have not gone unheard.

Tuncay expressed immense gratitude while reinforcing the necessity for a prompt response. We have endured suffering for too long, and unification with Hydronia offers my people a chance for revitalization and the return of democratic values, he explained earnestly.

Minister Erdermir listened intently as Tuncay continued to advocate for a transitional government that would pave the path toward democracy. Integrating Sakara into Hydronia will not be a simple task, the Minister cautioned, deliberating on the political, economic, and social ramifications that loomed large.

Tuncay understood the complexities but remained undeterred. Were here not just seeking assistance but are ready to rebuild Sakara together. We will fully commit to democratic principles and a partnership that encompasses all responsibilities, he assured, his resolve encapsulating the strength of his nation.

The mood in the room shifted from apprehension to cautious optimism. A glimpse of the potential for a partnership ignited hope among them. Tuncay proposed a plan to form a joint committee focusing on security, trade relations, and governance restructuringan approach that would stabilize Sakaras economy and foster mutual growth.

But President Zorlu also acknowledged potential skepticism from other nations regarding this unification. A strategic narrative needed to be crafted to position this partnership positively. Its imperative we frame this as a healing process rather than an annexation, he suggested, recognizing Tuncays vision required careful nurturing.

Absolutely! If we emphasize the humanitarian spirit of this union, we can quell concerns from the international community, Tuncay responded, his enthusiasm peaking. Together, we can cultivate an environment that fosters cooperation and security.

Minister Erdermir posited, A clear roadmap for integration is necessary. We need timelines for democratic elections and economic recovery. Additionally, we must schedule a press conference to communicate our intentions to the world.

Days turned into hours at the negotiation table, and optimism began to blossom as Tuncay and the Hydronic leaders crafted a comprehensive plan. By the end of their discussions, an agreement was forged. Sakara would become the 28th state of Hydronia, and Tuncay would serve as the first governor of this newly unified statea glorious triumph that once felt intangible.

The announcement of Sakaras integration reverberated throughout both nations, igniting widespread jubilation. From Hydropolis to the heart of Sakara, joyful celebrations erupted, underscoring the profound spirit of unity fostered amidst trials. In Sakaras streets, exuberant crowds waved flags adorned with traditional colors intertwined with the insignias of Hydronia, creating a vibrant mosaic of identity.
